messages.content:
The failing test calls ClassUtils.toClass with an Object array containing a mix of non-null and null elements: new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d }. The test expects the resulting Class array to be { String.class, null, Double.class }.

The implementation of ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]) iterates over the array and assigns classes[i] = array[i].getClass(). However, if array[i] is null, then calling getClass() on null causes a NullPointerException to be thrown.

This matches the issue described in the current bug report "c0.m0(Object[]) throws NPE on null array element", where c0.m0 corresponds to ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]).

The bug occurs because the method does not handle null array elements safely. Instead of checking if an element is null and placing null in the classes array, it directly calls getClass on the element, which is invalid for null.

Hence, the root cause is that ClassUtils.toClass does not check for null elements before calling getClass(), thereby causing a NullPointerException on null input elements.

No relevant information about this exact bug was found in the recent bug reports. They discuss other unrelated improvements.

Diagnosis:
The bug occurs because ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]) assumes elements are never null and directly invokes getClass() on each element without null checks. When a null element is present in the input array, this causes a NullPointerException. The failing test confirms this by passing an array with a null element. The method should be fixed to handle null elements gracefully by mapping them to null in the returned Class array instead of throwing.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
